clue.text: Some junk —— it's cheap, tawdry art

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the run of words that follows, a portion sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of junk, all of it's and the start of cheap

explanation.surface: A sneer at gaudy ornaments: cheap tawdry art is just so much junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a definition-plus-description, but junk, it's and cheap are only the string that hides the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is the usual label for showy, sentimental art of poor taste and little value.

clue.text: Divine humour from Irish comic heard on radio, initially

indicators.note: initially points at the beginnings of words, so only their opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the leading letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A heavenly sense of humour from an Irish comedian on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: Humour is not wit but one of the old bodily fluids; in Greek myth ichor flowed in the veins of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is the ethereal fluid said to run in the veins of the gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Hurry has spoilt barrelled beer

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the word before it loses its proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
beer is ale, and barrelled puts it inside a keg, a small barrel

explanation.surface: Someone has ruined a barrel of beer in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrelled works as a hidden container: the beer goes inside a keg, the small barrel the word implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake a leg is an informal command to hurry up and get moving.

clue.text: Permits a number to go with expedition

blocks.note: to have something is to allow it, as in 'I won't have it'
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Allowing some people to join an exploring expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Expedition is not a journey here but speed, the old sense of promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to move quickly, which is going with expedition in the sense of promptness.

clue.text: Want to mark the important place on map?

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
cities are the important places a map picks out

explanation.surface: Someone wishing to mark the key spot on a map, like a treasure hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Want looks like a verb of desire, but here it is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of shortage or lack of supplies is a direct synonym of scarcity.

clue.text: Aboard ship sailor smooths down bunk - that's standard

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so what follows sits within the ship's letters

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is a sailor
to sand wood is to smooth it
bunk and tripe both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: A sailor on a ship sanding down his berth to regulation standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunk is not a bed but nonsense, and standard is a flag. All three middle pieces go inside the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and the Stars and Stripes is the flag of the United States.

clue.text: Warning triangle set out

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so these letters are placed in a new arrangement

blocks.note: every letter used

explanation.surface: A motorist puts out a red warning triangle behind a broken-down car.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerting someone is giving them notice of danger, which is what warning means.

clue.text: Small character part provides relief

blocks.note: first meaning: a brief appearance by a notable actor
second meaning: a carving that stands out from its background

explanation.surface: A minor role in a play gives the audience some light relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief sounds like comic relief but is the sculptural sense, a raised design.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is both a brief star role in a film and a gem carved with a raised profile.

clue.text: Elevate film set and SF movie becomes suitable for screening

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the pieces means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: cine is the prefix for film, as in cine camera
to gel is to set firm, like a jelly
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A film set is raised and a sci-fi picture made fit for showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film set' reads as a studio stage, but film and set are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegenic describes someone who looks good on television, so suited to being shown on screen.

clue.text: Having lost a packet, he's a miser

indicators.note: something lost is mislaid and jumbled, so the words that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used as fodder

explanation.surface: A man who has lost a lot of money is now penny-pinching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost a packet' reads as the idiom for losing a lot of money; in fact 'Having lost' signals the anagram and 'a packet, he's' is the fodder. The words 'he's a' are used twice, once as fodder and once as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is an informal name for a stingy person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: Sounds like postman?

indicators.note: the clue says the word is judged by how it is heard, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: postman splits into post and man: post is what the postman delivers, also called mail, and man is the definition

explanation.walkthrough: Postman is one word in the surface but splits into post and man: post gives MAIL, which is said like MALE, and man is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is a male person, so the noun male can stand for him.

clue.text: Working to a T ensures accuracy

indicators.note: working suggests material being worked over and reshaped into a new form

blocks.note: the letter as printed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doing a job precisely, to a T, makes sure it is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working to a T' reads as the idiom for precision; the T is just one letter of the fodder added to ensures.
explanation.definitionFit: Trueness is the quality of being exact or correct, the same idea as accuracy.

clue.text: Depression as result of divorcing first husband

indicators.note: divorcing means parting company, and first says it is the earlier of two such letters that is separated off and dropped

blocks.note: through means by reason of, as in 'through no fault of his own'
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A low mood brought on by splitting up from one's first husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression suggests sadness after a divorce, but it is a dip in the ground, or a low-pressure area in weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a low-lying hollow or a long region of low atmospheric pressure, both kinds of depression.

clue.text: Secure release of disheartened saint

indicators.note: losing heart is read literally: the central letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: St Basil the Great, a fourth-century church father

explanation.surface: Arranging the release of a discouraged holy man from custody.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint is not ST here but a particular saint's name, which loses its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail someone is to obtain their temporary freedom from custody by paying a guarantee to the court.

clue.text: A produce store set up in stronghold

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a crop is farm produce
a silo is a store for grain

explanation.surface: Farm produce kept in a storehouse built inside a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified citadel on high ground in an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Game bird gets new home assembled on return

indicators.note: the pieces are put together and then the whole comes back the way it went, read from the end

blocks.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird
N is the abbreviation for new
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A game bird is shot and taken back home, assembled for the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Game bird looks like one phrase, but game is the definition and bird starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a bowling game in which nine wooden pins are knocked down by a ball.

clue.text: Common way to communicate official policy

blocks.note: first meaning: a telephone line shared by several subscribers
second meaning: the stance laid down by a political group

explanation.walkthrough: Common here means shared, the telephone line used by several households.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a shared telephone connection and the agreed position of a political organisation.

clue.text: Being so impassioned, affected even them

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so these letters are changed in order

blocks.note: every letter used

explanation.surface: Emotion so intense that it moved even them, the hardened ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means showing strong feeling, forceful and passionate in expression.

clue.text: What was made by Christian pair - a battle-axe?

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
a battle-axe is a fierce domineering woman, and so is an ogress

explanation.surface: A couple of Christians wondering what one of them made of a fearsome woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is the hero of Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, so what he made was progress on his journey to the Celestial City.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian, the pilgrim in Bunyan's allegory, makes progress, which gives the book its title.

clue.text: People take part in contest

blocks.note: first meaning: a group sharing descent, a nation or ethnic stock
second meaning: compete in a speed trial

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about entrants, but it splits after People.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a group of common ancestry, and the verb means to compete in a speed event.

clue.text: Bird and sheep frolic about

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: Birds and lambs gambolling around a spring meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To tittup is to prance or move in a lively, skittish way.

clue.text: Thin lengths of wood coming to a point

blocks.note: spars are long poles, such as masts and booms
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Thin poles of timber sharpened to a point, like stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A point here is a compass point, giving a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or meagre, as in sparse hair or a sparse crowd.

clue.text: Weapon left in general's keeping

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: rife means general or widespread
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gun left in the custody of an army general.
explanation.walkthrough: General is not an officer but the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a common kind of weapon.

clue.text: Way rhymes go round in time of need

blocks.note: surface reading: verses that go round and round
setter's reading: the nursery rhyme 'Rain, rain, go away, come again another day', where away rhymes with the last word

explanation.surface: Rhymes going round one's head when times are hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme asks the rain to go away and come again another day; the answer is the wet day it would rather avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for a rainy day means keeping money back for a future period of hardship.

clue.text: Greek story for Americans

blocks.note: first meaning: of Athens and its region, Attica
second meaning: the top floor of a house, story being the American spelling of storey

explanation.walkthrough: Story suggests a myth, but with the American spelling it is a floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means Athenian, and an attic is the top floor or room just under a roof.

clue.text: Cut reduced so sign on staff

indicators.note: reduced means cut down in size, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: cleft means split or cut in two

explanation.surface: Pay reduced, so the workforce carries placards: a story of staff cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff here is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Go into detail about right for emigrant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one expression wraps round the other

blocks.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Explaining at length about the rights an emigrant may have.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is someone living outside their native country, much like an emigrant who has left it.

clue.text: Incombustible mineral like tungsten extracted from gifts

indicators.note: extracted from means pulled out of, so one letter is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: as means like, in the way that
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten
to bestow is to give, so bestows means gifts as a verb

explanation.surface: A mineralogy note: a fireproof mineral, like tungsten, taken from rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Gifts looks like a plural noun but is the verb meaning gives, and tungsten is reduced to its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous silicate mineral once widely used because it does not burn.

clue.text: Speak earnestly and softly, and come across

blocks.note: p for piano, the musical direction to play softly
to reach a place is to get across to it

explanation.surface: Advice to a speaker: be earnest yet gentle, and get your point across.
explanation.walkthrough: Come across sounds like 'be understood', but it means arrive at, a sense of reach.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon or to urge moral views fervently on others.
